topics.title: The tigers' complaint and the king's first raid

concepts.learning_objective: Recall why the starving tigers appealed to their king and what they reported about Ajamil's sheep dog.
Interpret the irony in the tiger king's boastful solo raid and its humiliating result.

topics.title: The planned attack and the sheep dog's victory

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the tiger king's second plan of a mass attack led by himself.
Analyse how the poet uses hyperbole to show the sheep dog's speed and alertness.

topics.title: The tiger king's lies and Ajamil's pretence

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the hypocrisy in the tiger king's claim that the tigers came as friends.
Interpret why Ajamil pretended to believe the lies and avoided the sheep dog's eyes.

topics.title: The friendship treaty and the good shepherd

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the dinner, the long-term friendship treaty and the gifts Ajamil gave the tigers.
Evaluate the political wisdom behind Ajamil's decision that even tigers must eat.

topics.title: The poet, the form and the satire

concepts.learning_objective: State key facts about the poet Arun Kolatkar given in the chapter.
Distinguish the poem's literal and figurative levels as fable, allegory and satire.
